issues.legal_issue: A proposed arrangement that requires shareholder and court approval does not transfer rights in company property to its proposed beneficiaries before those approvals are obtained.
material_facts: The agreement proposed that the sale proceeds of company-owned shares be used to redeem preference shares, subject to the scheme being approved by shareholders and sanctioned by the court.
The board resolution likewise made distribution of the proceeds conditional on approval of the reduction of capital.
The required meetings and court sanction did not occur, and the scheme was never implemented.
issues.conclusion: The proposed preference-share beneficiaries acquired no rights in the shares or their sale proceeds; ownership remained with the company.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement and board resolution were proposals subject to the specified approvals. Until those conditions were met, the proposed scheme was inchoate and created no rights in the proposed beneficiaries. The Court considered the scheme in the context of Sections 153 and 185 of the Indian Companies Act; it relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.conditional_company_scheme: The company made a proposed arrangement under which beneficiaries would receive company property only if specified approvals were obtained.
predicates.required_approvals_not_obtained: The shareholders and court whose approvals were required did not approve the arrangement.

issues.definition: When a proposed company arrangement makes the transfer of company property conditional on approvals that are not obtained, its proposed beneficiaries acquire no rights to that property.

issues.legal_issue: In a winding-up summary application, company property held by the company's agents pending approval of a proposed scheme may be recovered by the official liquidator when the company is prima facie entitled to it.
material_facts: After a winding-up order, the official liquidator sought recovery of the proceeds from the sale of shares belonging to the company.
The board had directed the respondents to sell the shares and hold the proceeds pending approval of the proposed scheme.
The scheme was never approved or implemented, and the respondents retained the sale proceeds.
The respondents had no independent rights in the shares or proceeds; they held the proceeds for the company as its agents.
issues.conclusion: The respondents held the sale proceeds as agents of the company, and the official liquidator was entitled to recover them under Section 185 of the Indian Companies Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 185 of the Indian Companies Act authorizes the court, after a winding-up order, to require a listed person—including an agent of the company—to deliver money or property in that person's possession to the official liquidator when the company is prima facie entitled to it. The provision supplies a summary remedy for winding up the company's affairs. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.winding_up_summary_application: An official liquidator applies for summary recovery of property after the company has been ordered to wind up.
predicates.respondent_holds_company_property_as_age: The respondent holds property for the company as its agent rather than under an independent right.
predicates.company_is_prima_facie_entitled: The company appears entitled to the property on the facts before the court.

issues.definition: In a winding-up summary application, when a respondent holds property for the company as its agent and the company appears entitled to it, the official liquidator may recover the property summarily.
